summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted after experiencing a generalized seizure during hemodialysis, following recurrent coffee-ground emesis. She was found to be in nonconvulsive status epilepticus on EEG, and an MRI revealed possible subacute infarcts in the left frontal lobe, likely the seizure focus. She was treated with levetiracetam and phenytoin, later weaned to levetiracetam alone, with no further seizure activity. The coffee-ground emesis resolved spontaneously, and given stable hemoglobin, no endoscopy was performed. Hypoactive delirium improved after reducing her fentanyl patch dose from 75 to 62 mcg. Hypocalcemia was managed with IV calcium and adjustments to dialysis bath and medications. Wound care for calciphylaxis continued, and she remained on regular dialysis. She was discharged to an extended care facility on levetiracetam, pantoprazole, and optimized pain regimen, with follow-up planned in neurology and gastroenterology.
